findings.title: Every IN/memory hop is `leaked` on the production path: observe assumes per-request mention re-recording the harness never does
findings.claim: `_recall_request` (observe.py:393-407) looks for a MentionRecord of the FIRST message re-recorded at «the request after the last mention» and `_in_memory` (410-420) returns `leaked` when none exists. `GatewayV5._note_message_mentions` (harness.py:160-176) is called only from `_push` for the index just pushed, so a message is recorded exactly once, at its own request. The two never meet: with the real engine masking every user hop, all 48 IN/memory hops of 12 corpus memory cases print `leaked`. The corpus carries 540 IN/memory hops (of 11 514 IN hops), so `leak` and `coverage` are damned ~4.7pp corpus-wide and 100% on the memory_anaphora family for a gateway that leaked nothing.
findings.reproduction:
PYTHONPATH=. python3 /Users/igor/.claude/jobs/4e5fce9b/tmp/metrics-lens/memory_real.py
-> case memory_anaphora-000 requests 5
   mentions: [('i8', 1, 1, 'уваров владимир'), ('i9', 1, 1, '+79909637936'), ('i10', 2, 2, …), ('i11', 2, 2, …)]
   IN/user hops  : [('i8', 1, 'observed'), ('i9', 1, 'observed'), ('i10', 2, 'observed'), ('i11', 2, 'observed')]
   IN/memory hops: [('i9', 3, 'leaked'), ('i11', 4, 'leaked'), ('i10', 4, 'leaked'), ('i8', 5, 'leaked')]
   IN/memory statuses over 12 corpus memory cases (real engine, every user hop masked): {'leaked': 48}
   leak over IN/user+IN/memory: 48 / 96 | user-only leaked: 0 | memory leaked: 48
findings.proposed_fix: Decide the memory hop from what the harness actually records: the SDK holds the transcript, so «the substitute was carried forward» is exactly «the item was masked when its message was pushed and its substitute was not re-minted» — status = observed with produced = the item's (single) mention substitute, `leaked` only when the item has no mention at all or a later mention carries a different substitute; drop the request+1 arithmetic. Alternatively make `GatewayV5._push` re-record mentions for every message of the transcript on every request (it already re-masks the whole transcript), and then keep `_recall_request`. Add an observe test that builds mentions the way `_note_message_mentions` builds them (one per message) and demands `observed`.

findings.title: `value_matches` compares a per-LEAF hop against the WHOLE canonical: a perfect gateway tops out at 76.8% on round_trip / end_to_end / multi_all_out / doc_extracted / chain_value
findings.claim: The corpus declares OUT/tool_arg hops per leaf (`contact.last_name`, `address.street`, `to_location.city`, `passport.series`, 8 399 leaf-path hops, 0 parent paths) while every value metric calls `value_matches(item.type, leaf, item.canonical)` (metrics.py:236, 262, 460, 673) with the item's whole canonical. `fold('букин') != fold('букин сергей иванович')`; for LOC the city leaf is compared to nothing (city is dropped, roles from the right side must ALL match) so `to_location.city` is 0/189 by construction; CARD demands 16 solid digits vs a grouped canonical (54/84); clinic_book demands ISO vs 109 dotted DOB canonicals. Ceiling under a PERFECT gateway (leaf = the exact part the tool asks for): NAME 1620/2255, LOC 999/2019, PASSPORT 50/150, CARD 54/84, DOB 266/280, all 5968/7767 = 76.8%. The number the owner would publish as «round_trip» is capped at ~77% by the instrument, not the gateway.

findings.proposed_fix: Compare the leaf against the item's PART for the leaf's role (`spec_v5_for(tool, path).role` → `item.parts[role]`), digits-to-digits for PHONE/CARD/SNILS/INN, ISO-to-ISO for DOB, and the whole canonical only for a leaf whose FieldSpec has no role; never let a city leaf be judged by street/house/flat. findings.title: A passthrough gateway scores form_hOUT / chain_form / chain_value / multi_all_out 100%: `_out_call` and `_extra_call_hops` observe hops with nothing to compare
findings.claim: `_out_call` (observe.py:423-438) marks a declared OUT hop `observed` and calls form_match(restored, written) without asking whether `written` carried any substitute. When the gateway masked nothing (IN leaked) the agent writes the real value, `restored == written`, the verdict is `same`, and the hop is a HIT in form_hOUT, chain_form, retry_form, multi_all_out, chain_value (value_matches is then trivially true). `_extra_call_hops` (466-499) does the same for undeclared identity leaves, with `item_id=''` when no substitute spelling is found (490-492). The v5 headline line is therefore inflated by exactly the hops where the product failed on the way in. The same mechanism scores a FAKE that reached the tool with an empty engine residual report as form_hOUT 1/1 and residual 2/2 (probe g).

-> PASSTHROUGH gateway (masks nothing): leak 0/2 · coverage 0/2 · toolresult_masked 0/1 · form_hIN 0/0 · form_hOUT 3/3 · chain_value 1/1 · chain_form 1/1 · multi_all_out 1/1 · end_to_end 3/3 · residual 4/4
PYTHONPATH=. python3 /Users/igor/.claude/jobs/4e5fce9b/tmp/metrics-lens/observe_probes.py  (a) and (g)
-> (a) hop OUT/tool_arg status=observed produced='Иванова Елена' reference='Иванова Елена' same=True → form_hOUT 1/1
-> (g) FAKE in the tool, engine residual {} → hop observed produced='Пахомова Ольга' reference='Пахомова Ольга' same=True → form_hOUT 1/1, residual 2/2
findings.proposed_fix: An OUT hop is `observed` only when the written leaf contains a spelling (or ≥MIN_PIECE piece) of the item's substitute from `substitute_surfaces` — the observer already computes that set for the extra hops; otherwise status must be a new `unmasked` (nothing to compare, excluded from form_h* and chain_form, a miss in multi_all_out) and, when `restored == written` still contains a known substitute, `residual` regardless of what the engine reported. Add a passthrough fixture to form_hOUT / chain_form / multi_all_out expecting 0/n or н/п, never n/n.

findings.title: `residual` — the critical defect line — counts absent hops as clean and cannot see a substitute that survived declined, reformatted, or on an undeclared item
findings.claim: (1) `residual` hits = OUT hops with status != residual (metrics.py:683) so an `absent` hop is a HIT: an agent that calls nothing prints 4/4. (2) `residual_answer_items` (observe.py:330-345) matches only WHOLE surfaces the model READ inside `equal` regions; a substitute the model declined («Пахомовой Ольге») or reformatted («+7 (999) 000-11-22») and the engine failed to restore is invisible, and the declared answer hop then reads `absent` (= a residual HIT). (3) `_out_answer` (441-450) consults the residual set only for DECLARED hops and `_extra_answer_hops` (502-515) only walks replace spans, so an undeclared item's substitute standing verbatim in the customer's answer is found by `residual_answer_items` and then dropped — residual 1/1. In all three the fake reaches the customer and the line the docstring calls «THE critical defect» prints clean.
findings.reproduction:
PYTHONPATH=. python3 /Users/igor/.claude/jobs/4e5fce9b/tmp/metrics-lens/observe_probes.py
-> (b) agent called nothing, empty reply: hops OUT/tool_arg absent ×2, OUT/answer absent → residual 4/4
-> (e) reply_raw == reply == 'Передал Пахомовой Ольге, всё готово.' with substitutes {p1: 'Пахомова Ольга'}: residual_answer_items = frozenset() → OUT/answer status=absent → residual 2/2, answer_real 0/1
-> (f) undeclared answer item, 'Готово: Пахомова Ольга.' survived verbatim: residual_answer_items = {'p1'} → no hop emitted → residual 1/1
findings.proposed_fix: Count `absent` OUT hops in neither numerator nor denominator of `residual` (they are not leaves) — or as misses, never hits. Make the answer residual scan the WHOLE restored reply (not only equal regions) for every surface AND every ≥MIN_PIECE word-bounded piece of every substitute (the judge's `residual_pregate_of` already does this at judge.py:253-272 — reuse one rule), inflected forms included via the same stem trick `answer_spans` needs (see the answer-leg finding), and emit a `residual` hop for undeclared items too. Add fixtures: no-calls → 0/n or н/п; declined fake survived → 0/2; undeclared survived → 0/1.

findings.title: A missing or partial `<run>.hops.jsonl` silently empties every hop and makes `residual` certify cleanliness; the report is not marked НЕПОЛНЫЙ
findings.claim: `v5_observations` reads hops with `if hops_path.exists() else []` (report.py:231-232) and `hops.get(...,())` per case (245), so a run whose hops file is missing or truncated (a run that died between the arm write at harness.py:612 and the hop write at :614, or a copied directory) yields observations with zero hops. `residual` then prints len(observations)/len(observations) — «сертифицирует ≥» — while answer_real/leak/form_* print н/п and `SideBySide.incomplete` stays False. On a 1594-case run that is residual 1594/1594, certified ≥ 99.8%, from no data.
findings.reproduction:
PYTHONPATH=. python3 /Users/igor/.claude/jobs/4e5fce9b/tmp/metrics-lens/report_probes.py  (section 2)
-> with hops   : residual 3/3 сертифицирует ≥ 36.84% | answer_real 0/1 0.00%
   hops missing: residual 1/1 сертифицирует ≥  5.00% | answer_real н/п (нет применимых наблюдений)
   report incomplete flag: False | refused: {}
findings.proposed_fix: Raise ReportError when the hops file is absent, and refuse (or mark НЕПОЛНЫЙ and exclude) any (case, repeat) whose arm record exists but has no hop rows while the case declares hops; `residual`'s per-observation term must require at least one OUT hop declared or observed.

findings.title: The side-by-side «уровни v4» table is always empty except for levels whose TOST verdict is the one word «эквивалентно»: `_LEVEL_LINE` cannot match «НЕ эквивалентно» / «нет данных»

findings.title: The calibration stamp is trusted from the file: κ=0.21, the wrong judge model and prompt, `calibrated: true` prints «откалиброван» and the report is complete
findings.claim: `judge_half` (report.py:250-263) takes row 0 of `<run>.judge.jsonl` as the stamp and `side_by_side` sets `incomplete` from `stamp.calibrated` alone (308-311). `records.calibration_stamp_from_json` (records.py:405-420) reads the boolean as written; nobody re-derives it from `CalibrationThresholds`, and `calibration.is_current` (calibration.py:312-325, which checks judge_model/prompt_sha256 against the run) is never called from the report. findings.title: The answer leg reads a correctly restored declined or reformatted substitute as `absent`: answer_spans needles are whole surfaces and whole parts only
findings.claim: `answer_spans` attributes a replace region to an item only if a whole substitute surface or a whole `parts_of` part occurs in the raw reply (observe.py:277-296). The agent writes Russian: «Передал Пахомовой Ольге» (dative) or «+7 (999) 000-11-22» (reformatted); neither «Пахомова»/«Ольга» nor «9990001122» occurs, so the span is unattributed, the declared OUT/answer hop is `absent`, `answer_real` scores a miss, and form_hOUT never sees the answer hop — although the engine restored the reply correctly. Only surfaces the model READ (mentions) are known; a case the model chose itself is invisible. On a Russian corpus this is the common answer, not an edge.

-> (d2) raw 'Ваш номер +7 (999) 000-11-22 записан.' → restored '… +7 (916) 402-11-87 …': answer_spans = () → OUT/answer absent → answer_real 0/1
findings.proposed_fix: Add needles that survive inflection and notation: for NAME the first MIN_PIECE+ letters of each part as a word-prefix (stem) match («пахомов», «ольг»), for PHONE/CARD/SNILS/INN the digit signature of the raw region (`digits_of(raw[region]) == digits_of(surface)`), and let the replace region itself (the engine changed it) be attributed when exactly one item's stem/digits occur; keep `shared_block` for ambiguity. Add fixtures with a declined name and a reformatted phone expecting `observed`.

findings.title: `leak` counts absent IN/tool hops as protected: a passthrough whose agent never called the tool prints 2/3 while the only value shown leaked; the fixture pins the wrong denominator

The spec denominator is «all items shown to the model» (contracts.py:868); the fixture `fx_leak_adversarial` (fixtures.py:245-253) expects 2/2 — encoding the inflation as the norm. An agent that acts less raises the gateway's leak line; the memory-hop and `_in_memory` `absent` branches (observe.py:413-414) feed the same term.

The corpus declares `source_hop` on answer hops, so 56% of the chain denominator is the answer leg — where `produced` is an alignment window and `value_matches` against the slot text is a different question from «tool B got A's value». The spec row names «A→B transitions» (contracts.py:883-884) and the docstring names «a tool fed its own result back».

findings.title: `multi_consistency` counts two inflections of ONE substitute as two substitutes
findings.claim: `substitute_surfaces` (observe.py:123-135) deliberately returns every inflected spelling the model read as surfaces of one substitute; `multi_consistency` (metrics.py:481-485) then counts DISTINCT spellings seen across the turn's calls and fails the turn on >1. A turn that writes «Пахомова Ольга» into a name field and «перезвонить Пахомовой Ольге» into a note is scored as a re-mint — on the family this line exists for.

findings.proposed_fix: Count distinct substitutes by their MINT (the `substitutes[item]` surface / vault key), not by spelling: a spelling is a hit if its nominative fold or its ≥MIN_PIECE stems match the minted surface; only a spelling that shares no stem with the minted substitute is a second substitute. Fixture: two inflections → 1/1.

The observer's own docstring (observe.py:27-33) refuses exactly this for the answer leg. I showed the metric consequence (probe g: an empty report scores the fake as form_hOUT 1/1, residual clean) but did not produce an engine miss; whether `residual_tokens` misses a transliterated / initial / typo'd substitute in a tool leaf is the engine's question.

findings.what_i_could_not_break: Coverage vs overlap on the tool leg held: `covering_piece` demands full cover and `_surviving_piece` scans the whole masked text; a piece covering all but the surname is `leaked` (test_observe.test_leaked_in_partial_cover) and a surviving city is exempt. `coverage` does not fire on the engine's own substitutes sharing the real given name — 0/40 fresh vaults minted a «…Елена» for «Иванова Елена». `value_matches` casefold + ё→е is accepted by ruling R-36 (the only hidden change it buys is «Фёдорович»→«Федорович», which form_match also cannot see — noted, not ranked). `form_match` abstain did not hide a difference I could build: a letterless or Latin produced string still differs on order/parts; PHONE `other`/DOB `other` differ from real shapes; the isolation pairs in test_form hold. `answer_real` treats one residual among four data as a miss (fixture). Clopper–Pearson and `zero_failure_floor` (alpha^(1/n), one-sided) are right and «100%» is never printed. `Line(0,0)` renders н/п everywhere. A metric that raises is a refusal, not a crash (test_report_gate). The v4 block itself is v4's own `_load_run → score_triples → render` bytes (only the re-rendered level table inside the fence is v5's, and empty). `merged_v5_records` keeps a failed arm's row and `_guarded_arm_v5` always writes `_empty_run`, so a dead arm's declared hops become absent misses rather than vanishing (given the hops file is written — see the blocker). Missing corpus.v5.json is a ReportError; a judge file with no stamp marks НЕПОЛНЫЙ. `consistency` can genuinely fire on the engine: one conversation minted «770-310-540 64» for a SNILS in a message and «094-489-004 28» for the same SNILS in a JSON tool result (notation_mint.py) — an engine defect outside this lens, but proof the line is an instrument. findings.title: 42% of the revised half's declared IN/tool hops are crossings the mock never renders, and `leak` scores every one of them as a SUCCESS
findings.claim: `leak` (the headline «values the gateway altered before the model saw them») counts an IN hop with status `absent` as a hit: `sum(1 for _one, hop in rows if hop.status != "leaked")` over ALL IN hops. `observe._in_tool` (observe.py:380-385) returns `absent` when the tool result carries no slot for the item. In the revised half 1694 of 3998 declared IN/tool hops can never be tagged: `mock._retag` (mock.py:453) replaces v4's private slot tags by a BY-VALUE lookup (`_tag_for_value`, mock.py:388), and `seed_item` (mock.py:294) deletes from that index any value two items share — which is exactly the construction of `compare-*` (three suggestions on one street) and `lookup_list-*` (three Букины). 1360 of the 3998 hops sit on a value the case itself repeats, so they are untaggable by ANY agent. Result: ≥14.7% of `leak`'s corpus-wide denominator (11514 IN hops/repeat) is free credit that no gateway earned. `residual` (metrics.py:677) has the same shape — an absent OUT hop is a hit. Every phantom was on a tool the control agent DID call, so this is tagging, not agent behaviour.

findings.title: 10 chain transitions compare two different data of one person, and 60 IN/memory hops name a seed item the mention log may never carry
findings.claim: R06 allows an OUT hop's `source_hop` to point at an IN hop «of the SAME item or of an item of the same identity», and `chain_value` then compares `hop.produced` with `source.reference` as if they were one datum. In `user_in_loop-*`, hop 10 (`clinic_book.patient.first_name`, item i2 «сергей») sources hop 3 (the IN/tool hop of item i1 «букин»), so the metric compares the restored first name against the surname's span — 10 such transitions, all same-type, so no type check can see them. Separately, 60 IN/memory hops (all in `user_in_loop`) name a SEED item: `observe._in_memory` (observe.py:410-421) resolves them through `run.mentions`, whose seed-item entries carry `msg=-1`, and its `first_msg`/`request_index` matching was written for message mentions; the hop reads `absent` whenever the arithmetic misses, and an absent IN hop is a `leak` hit (finding 1).
findings.proposed_fix: Tighten R06 to «the SAME item», and give a leaf fed by a sibling field of one record its own IN hop rather than borrowing the neighbour's. For the memory hops, either declare them only on message items (the anaphora family's own shape) or give `_in_memory` an explicit branch for a value the agent learned from a tool result, so «recalled from a tool result» and «never observed» are two statuses rather than one.

findings.what_i_could_not_break: Held up under attack: (1) **The document family.** All 375 `extracted_item_ids` across the 100 document cases are actually tagged in the rendered file — csv/free_text/form/scan all 25 each, `file_read`/`form_parse` driven with the seeded path/text, 0 missing. `DocumentSpec.record_ids` vs `record_count` (ruling R-30) is respected. (2) **`memory_anaphora`'s R16.** 0 of the 480 MemorySpecs re-write the value at `recall_turn` when `anaphora != 'none'` — checked against the message text for the whole value and for every part longer than 3 characters; all four anaphora kinds are present 120 times each and every memory item has a message locus. (3) **`retry_same_tool`.** All 360 declared IN hops render once the scripted `ForcedError` fires and the second call is made; `seed_backend_v5` refuses a forced error with no canonical to echo (mock.py:1265-1270), and R-19's «echo the canonical, never the spoken surface» holds in the data. (4) **`same_tool_other_target`.** 0 of 50 cases let the two targets share a value of any type — the one family whose construction genuinely guarantees the cross-contamination it tests. (5) **The OUT-owner table.** 0 hops corpus-wide disagree with `contracts.hop_owner_of_leaf`, so `observe._out_call`'s `ObserveError` never fires; `TEMPLATE_FIELDS`/`SUMMARY_FIELDS` file every free leaf of every tool in `REGISTRY_V5`, and `OUT/template` (296) and `OUT/summary` (336) both clear `MIN_TYPE_DENOMINATOR`. (6) **Today's ladder.** `ladder.corpus_sha256` matches the corpus on disk, no tier holds an id the corpus lacks, and the holdout is 319/1594 = 20.01% — the freeze is broken as a mechanism (finding 5), not as a fact. (7) **The files agree with each other.** `corpus.v5.json` round-trips to its own digest, and `corpus.json` is the same objects' `.base`. (8) **The engine-import ban.** Only `harness.py` reaches `pseudex`; every module I imported in this audit loaded without it. (9) **The suite is green**: `test_build`, `test_revise`, `test_schema`, `test_metrics`, `test_observe`, `test_fixtures` all PASS, so nothing above is an already-known red. I did **not** build a synthetic worthless corpus that passes K01–K15 from scratch — I got the same result on the real one (findings 3 and 7: 132 hollow `has_result` cases and 1215 wrong return forms, both accepted silently), so the K rules demonstrably score declarations rather than crossings, but a purpose-built minimal counterexample is still unwritten. I also could not run the live agent (no model calls allowed), so every «what the agent does» claim here is either agent-independent (role contradictions, ambiguous tags, ladder staleness) or measured with v4's deterministic control arm under two policies.

findings.lens: THE HARNESS, THE JUDGE AND THE STREAMING LEG — does the run take the engine's production path, and does the judge see exactly what the client sees and nothing more?

findings.title: The streaming leg is measured on every streaming case and read by nothing; the 84 streaming cases are scored on text the streaming customer never sees
findings.claim: `run_arm_v5` restores a streaming case's answer twice — whole (`unmask_text`) and through the sidecar's chunk contract (`StreamDetokenizer` at 17 chars) — then puts the WHOLE restoration into `base.reply` (harness.py:391) and the disagreement into `stream_mismatch` (harness.py:408). `stream_mismatch` is written to `<run>.arms.v5.jsonl` (records.py:239) and is read by NO metric, NO axis and NO report line: it appears in no `MetricSpec` of `contracts.METRICS` (contracts.py:857-894), in no key of `metrics.METRIC_FUNCTIONS` (metrics.py:691), in no entry of `contracts.AXES` (contracts.py:903), and nowhere in `report.py`. Meanwhile every OUT/answer hop is derived from `run.base.reply` (observe.py:283, 338, 446, 513), so `form_hOUT`, `answer_real`, `residual` and the judge (`judge_input` -> `run.base.reply`) all score the whole-text restoration. On a streaming case with a real chunk-leg defect the report therefore prints the product as correct on an answer the customer read wrong, and the one number that would have said otherwise is thrown away. This is exactly the defect class CLAUDE.md records for `Case.negatives` and `FieldSpec.required`: declared, written, read by nobody. Scale: 84 streaming cases (5.3% of 1594; 69 of the `large` tier), a floor the corpus builder enforces (`MIN_STREAMING_CASES = 60`, contracts.py:460, rule K11), and on the corpus's own streaming cases the two restorations really do disagree at 4.0%. RULINGS R-46 says «stream_mismatch is the metric that carries it» — there is no such metric.

findings.title: A residual substitute in any non-final turn raises OracleLeak on the production path and kills the whole live run; 62 of 66 multi-turn cases sampled are one agent restatement away from it
findings.claim: `dialogue_context` puts `ArmRunV5.turn_replies` into the judge's dialogue section (judge.py:321-374) and `build_prompt` runs `assert_blind` over that section (judge.py:391). The module docstring exempts only the ANSWER («tripping the guard on it would crash a paid run over a defect the instrument is built to measure») — the same defect one turn earlier is not exempt and raises `OracleLeak`. `harness.judge_triple` (harness.py:443) has no `except`, so the exception leaves `run_triple_v5` after all three arms have been paid for, leaves `drive_v5`'s `worker` before ANY row is appended, and leaves `main()` before `finish_run`, `stamp_judge_file` and `meta.json`: the run dies with no report, no gate file, no calibration stamp, and the failing triple leaves no row at all — so `--resume` will re-pay for it and hit the same leak for ever. Worse, `input_sha256` (harness.py:459/462) calls `build_prompt` a second time even when the residual pre-gate has ALREADY refused the case, so a case the judge was never going to be asked about still crashes. Reachability is not theoretical: the engine does not restore a lower-cased substitute (the form it mints for the corpus's `chat`/`sloppy`/`voice_raw`/`voice_itn` registers), so an agent that restates a value in the register it read it in leaves a whole substitute standing. In a 150-case random sample, 62 of the 66 multi-turn cases carry at least one such substitute.

findings.title: The calibration sheet hands the human labeller the judge's own label and reason, so the κ that gates publication is measured against an anchored rater
findings.claim: `sheet_rows` writes `judge_label=label, judge_reason=reason` into the very row whose `human_label` the human is about to fill (calibration.py:412-423). `judge_reason` carries the judge's verbatim quote and rationale, i.e. maximum anchoring. Cohen's κ and raw agreement are agreement between two INDEPENDENT raters; the sheet destroys that independence, and there is no blind mode — `calibration export` has no flag for it (calibration.py:448-472). Both numbers gate the report: `stamp()` sets `calibrated` from `raw >= 0.85` and `kappa >= 0.70` (calibration.py:296-307), `report.judge_half` reads the stamp and the header prints «НЕ ОТКАЛИБРОВАН» when it is false (report.py:328-330), and the module docstring says a report with an uncalibrated judge is not circulated. The instrument's own doctrine — «a `none` verdict counts as a DISAGREEMENT, it is not dropped», «κ is 0.0 when a rater is constant» — is careful about everything except whether the human saw the answer first.

findings.title: `repeat_disagreement` is structurally 0.0: the K stability rows of one answer all carry a single judge label, so the threshold that gates publication can never fire
findings.claim: `repeat_check` is defined as «share of answers whose K judge labels are NOT all equal» (calibration.py:270-279) and `stamp` refuses a judge whose spread exceeds `CALIBRATION.max_repeat_disagreement = 0.1` (calibration.py:302-307). But the harness asks the judge exactly ONCE per (case, repeat) — `judge_triple` is called once in `run_triple_v5` (harness.py:556) — and `judge_labels_of` therefore holds one (label, reason) per (case_id, repeat) (calibration.py:371-383). `sheet_rows` looks that single entry up for EVERY row of the sample, including the `repeat_index` 1..K-1 rows `draw_repeats` produced (calibration.py:402-423), so all K labels of a `sample_id` are identical by construction and `repeat_check` returns 0.0 on anything the pipeline can produce. The only place a non-zero spread exists is `test_calibration._stable_repeats(..., disagreeing=1)` (test_calibration.py:73-81), which assigns «выдумал» to repeat rows by hand — a fixture no live run could ever generate. That is precisely the shape CLAUDE.md warns about («an instrument that cannot fail is not an instrument»), and it sits in the same `stamp()` that the docstring defends so carefully for the MISSING-sub-sample case.

findings.title: The rubric's form guard cannot catch its own subject: it misses every synonym the rubric itself uses, and fires on «информация»
findings.claim: `_FORBIDDEN_IN_RUBRIC = ("падеж", "регистр", "формат", "форма")` is a four-stem substring test over `RUBRIC + HEADINGS`, run at import so that «the rule the judge does not grade spelling is worth exactly as much as the mechanism that keeps it true» (judge.py:145-153). The mechanism is a word list, and the rubric's OWN sentence about form passes it only because it reaches for synonyms — «склонение, заглавные буквы, разделители, порядок слов». Any later edit worded the same way turns the judge into a form judge with the guard green: «проверь склонение фамилии», «проверь заглавные буквы в имени», «оцени, верно ли просклонено имя», «проверь написание значения» all pass. It also fires in the wrong direction: «информация» contains «форма», so an innocuous rubric line mentioning «всю информацию диалога» raises `RuntimeError` at import and the module will not load. The guard is polarity-blind too — it cannot tell «you do NOT judge падеж» from «judge падеж».

findings.proposed_fix: Stop guarding the prose and guard the CONTRACT instead: pin `prompt_sha256()` (rubric + headings) to a literal in `test_judge.py`, so any edit to the rubric is a red test that a human must read and re-bless — which is the only check that survives synonyms. findings.title: `pregate_with` and `judge_with` are unreachable adapters, and a docstring states the harness uses one of them
findings.claim: `judge.py:285` says «`pregate_with` is what the harness uses», but `harness.judge_triple` calls `residual_pregate_of` directly (harness.py:450) and `judge_answer` directly (harness.py:452); `pregate_with` (judge.py:288) and `judge_with` (judge.py:503) have no callers anywhere in the package or its tests. The `contracts.ResidualPregate` and `contracts.Judge` protocols are therefore satisfied only by functions nothing on the production path invokes, and the two-argument `residual_pregate` exists solely for one line of `test_judge.py:210`. A reader tracing «who applies the pre-gate with the case's real parts» is sent to a dead function.

Keeping an adapter nobody calls beside a docstring that says it is the one in use is how a protocol drifts from the code that is supposed to satisfy it.

findings.what_i_could_not_break:
**The gateway arm really is the production path.** I drove 40 real corpus cases through `GatewayV5` offline with `testkit.load_dev_bundle()` and found no second minting path: `tools()` goes through `envelope.mask_tools`, every message and every tool result through `envelope.mask_messages` (`RealGateway._push`, gateway.py:154-175), tool arguments through `redact.unmask_arguments` and never through the chunk path, the final reply through `redact.unmask_text`/`StreamDetokenizer`, and one in-memory `Vault` per triple reached through `for_conversation`. v4's double-pass check (`score._mask_message` vs the envelope output, byte for byte, gateway.py:169-173) is still armed and raises `HarnessError` on any divergence — it is the strongest single guarantee in the rig.

**The controls are v4's.** `run_triple_v5` calls `v4_harness._guarded_arm` with v4's `PassThrough` for both C and C′ (harness.py:546, 552-554), so `_options`, `cap_usd`, `_timeout`, `session_id`, `_termination` and the `ArmRun`/`ArmMeta` record are v4's own bytes. The one difference — all three arms run against `seed_backend_v5` — is required (one mock, three arms) and is the right call.

**The record wiring is correct where it is easiest to get wrong.** `control_reply` carries the **C** arm's reply (not C′) of the *same* triple; `turn_replies` are the I arm's own, restored, one per user message, aligned from the front; `dialogue_context`'s dropped "evidence" turn is computed the same way `run_arm_v5` picks `raw_reply`, so the answer is never quoted to the judge twice; `call_turns`/`ordinal` are computed in an await-free window so a concurrent tool call cannot desynchronise them; `request_count` correctly skips the system prompt (harness.py:143-147).

**The blind guard does work on whole substitutes.** Across the 40 real gateway passes, every prompt that `build_prompt` actually produced carried zero whole substitutes and zero substitute *pieces* (checked with `parts_of` over `PIECE_TYPES` at `MIN_PIECE`, word-boundary anchored). The prompts that did not get produced raised `OracleLeak` — which is finding 2, not a leak.

**The judge's SDK seam is real, not aspirational.** Against `claude_agent_sdk` 0.2.82 every option `judge._options` passes exists (`output_format`, `setting_sources`, `max_budget_usd`, `strict_mcp_config`, `continue_conversation`), `permission_mode="dontAsk"` is a valid `PermissionMode`, and `ResultMessage.structured_output` exists — so the judge is not silently unusable in a way the offline tests would hide. `setting_sources=[]` and `cwd=tempfile.gettempdir()` do keep this repository's CLAUDE.md away from the judge.

**One ledger, and it is honest during a run.** `SpendLedger` holds `committed + reserved <= ceiling` at every instant across the agent and the judge; `test_ledger_shared` proves identity *and* drives a zero-ceiling triple to watch it be recorded as refused rather than dropped. `run_triple_v5`'s `finally` settles even on an exception.

**Record invariants hold.** `judged_by == "none"` ⇔ empty label is enforced on read (records.py:337-345); `status == "observed"` ⇔ a form verdict exists is enforced on read (records.py:443-446); the v5 block round-trips `turn_replies`/`mentions`/`tool_results`/`stream_mismatch` losslessly, and the scrub path keeps counts while dropping text.

**The import fence holds both halves.** `pseudex_importers` walks with `ast` (not grep), the module list is exactly `("harness",)` and the test list exactly `["test_harness_stream"]`, and a planted leaky file is found — I re-ran it.

Two things I looked at and decided were not defects: *one carry per `choice.index`* is not exercised at all (the SDK agent produces a single stream, so there is nothing to interleave) — a coverage gap in the product's contract rather than a bug in the rig; and `RealGateway` hardcoding `org_id="agentpii4"` for the `MaskContext` while v5 builds `Vault(":memory:", "agentpii5")` is cosmetic here, because the cache, audit and vault objects are all fresh per triple — but a v5 run's audit rows do say `agentpii4`.

finding.title: Every IN/memory hop is `leaked` on the production path: observe assumes per-request mention re-recording the harness never does
finding.claim: `_recall_request` (observe.py:393-407) looks for a MentionRecord of the FIRST message re-recorded at «the request after the last mention» and `_in_memory` (410-420) returns `leaked` when none exists. `GatewayV5._note_message_mentions` (harness.py:160-176) is called only from `_push` for the index just pushed, so a message is recorded exactly once, at its own request. The two never meet: with the real engine masking every user hop, all 48 IN/memory hops of 12 corpus memory cases print `leaked`. The corpus carries 540 IN/memory hops (of 11 514 IN hops), so `leak` and `coverage` are damned ~4.7pp corpus-wide and 100% on the memory_anaphora family for a gateway that leaked nothing.
finding.reproduction:

-> case memory_anaphora-000 requests 5
   mentions: [('i8', 1, 1, 'уваров владимир'), ('i9', 1, 1, '+79909637936'), ('i10', 2, 2, …), ('i11', 2, 2, …)]
   IN/user hops  : [('i8', 1, 'observed'), ('i9', 1, 'observed'), ('i10', 2, 'observed'), ('i11', 2, 'observed')]
   IN/memory hops: [('i9', 3, 'leaked'), ('i11', 4, 'leaked'), ('i10', 4, 'leaked'), ('i8', 5, 'leaked')]
   IN/memory statuses over 12 corpus memory cases (real engine, every user hop masked): {'leaked': 48}
   leak over IN/user+IN/memory: 48 / 96 | user-only leaked: 0 | memory leaked: 48
finding.proposed_fix: Decide the memory hop from what the harness actually records: the SDK holds the transcript, so «the substitute was carried forward» is exactly «the item was masked when its message was pushed and its substitute was not re-minted» — status = observed with produced = the item's (single) mention substitute, `leaked` only when the item has no mention at all or a later mention carries a different substitute; drop the request+1 arithmetic. Alternatively make `GatewayV5._push` re-record mentions for every message of the transcript on every request (it already re-masks the whole transcript), and then keep `_recall_request`. Add an observe test that builds mentions the way `_note_message_mentions` builds them (one per message) and demands `observed`.

Every reproduction is a throwaway script under /Users/igor/.claude/jobs/4e5fce9b/tmp/metrics-lens/ run as `cd /Users/igor/Projects/Obscura/prototype && source .venv/bin/activate && PYTHONPATH=. python3 <script>`; nothing under prototype/ was edited; no model, no network (memory_real.py and notation_mint.py load the dev bundle and run the engine in-process).

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED — and it is stronger than the finding states: for a large block of hops NO string can satisfy both the tool and the metric.

WHAT I VERIFIED (all reproducible, all read-only)

1. The comparison is leaf-vs-whole-canonical, by construction.
- prototype/bench/agentpii5/observe.py:434-437 sets `produced = leaf_text(flatten(call.restored), hop.tool_name, hop.path)`; observe.py:153-154 returns the SCALAR at `path` when the path is present in the flattened call. So `produced` is the leaf.
- prototype/bench/agentpii5/metrics.py:108 `value_matches(pii_type, produced, target)` is called with `item.canonical` as `target` at metrics.py:236 (round_trip), :262 (round_trip_repaired), :420 (chain_value), :460 (multi_all_out), :673 (doc_extracted), and end_to_end at metrics.py:487.
- Corpus check (my own script, /Users/igor/.claude/jobs/4e5fce9b/tmp/verify-lens/probe1.py): 7767 declared OUT/tool_arg hops, 7767 leaf paths, 0 parent paths. 1862 of them declare a leaf whose FieldSpec `role` is ONE part of a MULTI-part item canonical.

2. MUTUAL EXCLUSIVITY — the decisive test the finding did not run. I fed both candidate strings to the mock's OWN parsers (bench/agentpii4/tools.py) and to `value_matches`:
  person.last_name, canonical 'букин сергей иванович': 'букин' → tool ACCEPTED / value_matches False; 'букин сергей иванович' → tool REFUSED `name_cyrillic` / value_matches True.
  passport.series, canonical '3619 141783': '3619' → ACCEPTED / False; '3619 141783' → REFUSED `series_format` / True.
  clinic_book.patient.birth_date (FieldSpec role='iso'), canonical '14.03.1987': '1987-03-14' → ACCEPTED / False; '14.03.1987' → REFUSED `date_not_iso8601` / True.
So for NAME split leaves, PASSPORT series/number and clinic_book DOB the metric demands exactly the string the tool rejects. Those hops are 0 for ANY gateway, perfect or not. (CARD is the one weak row: `parse_card` accepts both groupings, so its 54/84 is a notation choice, not an impossibility.)

3. LOC is 0 by construction, and the instrument rewards wrong behaviour. `value_matches` (metrics.py:115-119) drops `city` and requires street/house/flat from the right side to ALL match. `parts_of("LOC","брянск")` → {'street':'брянск'} vs `parts_of("LOC","брянск проспект загорондый 199 квартира 109")` → {'street':'брянск загорондый','house':'199','flat':'109'} → False. I confirmed 189 cases where ONE item is declared at TWO leaves of the SAME call — `to_location.address` AND `to_location.city` (e.g. case `summary-000`, item i4) — so the city leaf is 0/189 unless the agent writes the whole address into the city field, which the tool's form comparator and the CRM would both call wrong.

4. Ceiling reproduced. `PYTHONPATH=. python3 /Users/igor/.claude/jobs/4e5fce9b/tmp/metrics-lens/ceiling2.py` → 5968/7767 = 76.8%; by type NAME 1620/2255, LOC 999/2019, PASSPORT 50/150, CARD 54/84, DOB 266/280. Discounting CARD as notation-only, the provably unsatisfiable core is ~1769 hops, i.e. the ceiling is ≤77.2% however the gateway writes a card. The number is right within a point.

NOT BY DESIGN, NOT BY RULING
- RULINGS.md mentions `value_matches` once, at line 220, and only to accept «casefold + ё→е». No ruling addresses leaf-vs-canonical. R-19 (line 98) is about `ForcedError` echoing the canonical, a different surface.
- docs/tz-agentpii5.md §4.2 (line 167) calls `round_trip` «абсолют» and §8.3's table gives «реал» as the passing column; nothing licenses comparing a surname leaf to a full FIO.
- schema.py's `validate_v5`/`validate_corpus_v5` contain no rule tying a hop's leaf role to the item's canonical, so `build --check` cannot see it either.
- The instrument's own fixtures hide it: fixtures.py:215 `OUT_ARG` uses `crm_upsert_contact` path `contact.name` — a WHOLE-name leaf on a whole-name item — so every round_trip/end_to_end fixture is the one shape where leaf == canonical. `python3 -m bench.agentpii5.test_metrics` is green (PASS) with the defect present.

ONE PARTIAL DEFENCE, AND WHY IT DOES NOT SAVE IT
fixtures.py:319-332 deliberately scores ISO at `clinic_book.patient.birth_date` as 0/1 («a repaired value is not a round trip»). That intent is real, but it was written against a leaf that can ONLY be ISO — the tool refuses the dotted form — so the line is a constant 0 there rather than a judgement. CLAUDE.md's «an instrument that cannot fail is not an instrument» has an exact mirror here: an instrument that cannot pass is not one either.

SEVERITY: blocker. `round_trip` and `end_to_end` are the headline lines of v5 («шлюз не ломает агента»), and both are capped near 77% by the corpus/metric pairing rather than by the gateway. v5 has not been run live yet, so no number is published — fixing it now costs one comparator and one corpus-level self-check, while publishing 77% as a gateway result would be a false statement about the product. The PROPOSED FIX is right in direction (compare against `item.parts[spec_v5_for(tool, path).role]`, digits-to-digits, ISO-to-ISO, whole canonical only when the FieldSpec has no role) and the pinning self-check it asks for — «a perfect gateway scores 1.0 on every declared hop» — is the part that must land, because without it the same drift returns silently. Two corpus facts the fix must also handle: (a) the corpus is inconsistent about item granularity (NAME surname leaves: 399 multi-part items vs 302 single-part), and (b) `crm_upsert_contact` declares city/house/flat leaves against items whose canonical is street-only ('толстого' with parts city='омск'), which is a corpus defect the new self-check would expose rather than a comparator issue.

finding.title: A passthrough gateway scores form_hOUT / chain_form / chain_value / multi_all_out 100%: `_out_call` and `_extra_call_hops` observe hops with nothing to compare
finding.claim: `_out_call` (observe.py:423-438) marks a declared OUT hop `observed` and calls form_match(restored, written) without asking whether `written` carried any substitute. When the gateway masked nothing (IN leaked) the agent writes the real value, `restored == written`, the verdict is `same`, and the hop is a HIT in form_hOUT, chain_form, retry_form, multi_all_out, chain_value (value_matches is then trivially true). `_extra_call_hops` (466-499) does the same for undeclared identity leaves, with `item_id=''` when no substitute spelling is found (490-492). The v5 headline line is therefore inflated by exactly the hops where the product failed on the way in. The same mechanism scores a FAKE that reached the tool with an empty engine residual report as form_hOUT 1/1 and residual 2/2 (probe g).

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED by my own reproduction, not the one handed to me.

WHAT I RAN (scratch only, nothing in the repo touched):
/Users/igor/.claude/jobs/4e5fce9b/tmp/verify-passthrough/probe.py and probe2.py — built from bench/agentpii5/fixtures.py builders (_case/_hop/_item/_call/_run/_with_calls/_with_subs/_with_results) and driven through the real observe() and the real metrics functions. `cd prototype && source .venv/bin/activate && PYTHONPATH=. python3 …`.

probe.py, arm B (the gateway minted no substitute for the item — a detection miss; the agent read and wrote the real value; /unmask_arguments left it alone so restored == written):
  IN/user status='leaked' produced='' reference='Иванова Елена'
  OUT/tool_arg status='observed' produced='Иванова Елена' reference='Иванова Елена' same=True
  leak 0/1 · coverage 0/1 · form_hIN 0/0 · form_hOUT 1/1 · residual 2/2
probe2.py:
  (1) chain A→B, nothing masked: chain_value 1/1 · chain_form 1/1 · form_hOUT 1/1, while leak 0/1 and toolresult_masked 0/1.
  (2) two arguments in one turn, nothing masked: multi_all_out 1/1 · form_hOUT 2/2.
  (3) the FAKE reached the tool and the engine reported residual {}: hop observed, produced==reference=='Пахомова Ольга', same=True → form_hOUT 1/1 · residual 2/2.

MECHANISM, WITH LINES. prototype/bench/agentpii5/observe.py:423-438 `_out_call`: after `call_for_hop`, it reads `written` and `restored` (431-433), asks only `_has_residual(call, hop.path)` (436) — i.e. the ENGINE's own residual report (observe.py:162-165) — and otherwise returns `_observed(...)` (438), which attaches `form_match(produced, reference)` (observe.py:354-359). Nothing asks whether `written` ever carried a substitute. `_extra_call_hops` (observe.py:466-499) repeats it for undeclared identity leaves, with `item_id=''` when no spelling of any substitute is found (489-492), status 'observed' at 495-498. Downstream every form line then counts the hop: metrics.py:351-355 (form_hOUT), 424-431 (chain_form), 409-421 (chain_value — `value_matches(hop.produced, source.reference)` is trivially true when both are the real value), 448-463 (multi_all_out).

NOT BY DESIGN, NOT BY RULING.
- RULINGS.md R-01…R-46: no ruling touches hop status, form_hOUT, passthrough or an unmasked OUT leaf (grepped the whole 288-line file for leaked/form_h/hop/unmasked — only R-13/R-25/R-31/R-41 mention hops, on unrelated matters).
- The spec is against the code: docs/tz-agentpii5.md:36-43 defines a hop as «один переход значения ПД ЧЕРЕЗ ШЛЮЗ» and the OUT check as `form(реал) == form(подмены, как её написал агент)`; §4.3 line 293 counts «e, у которых form_match == same». With nothing masked there is no «подмена, как её написал агент», so the code is not computing the spec's comparison — it computes form(real) == form(real).
- contracts.py:1080-1084 is normative and argues the other way: `leaked` exists precisely because «the real value reached the model unaltered — NO FORM TO COMPARE», and `observed` is documented as «compared». The vocabulary (HOP_STATUSES, contracts.py:1098) simply has no OUT counterpart — exactly the gap the proposed fix names.
- observe.py's own module docstring, rule 3 (lines 23-27), calls emitting a hop «observed with nothing to compare» v4's D1 defect. `_out_call` does that.

WHY NO TEST CATCHES IT. The report gate (report.py:85-120) runs each metric against fixtures.py fixtures that are hand-built HopObservations via `_seen` — it never calls `observe`, so the observer's status decision is unreachable from the gate. Worse, fixtures.py:602-605 (`_multi_all_out_fixtures`) uses `_seen(case, first, "NAME", REAL_NAME, REAL_NAME)` — produced == reference — inside BOTH the zero and the one fixture, so the exact shape at issue is baked in as a hit. test_observe.py pins `leaked` for the IN side (test_in_orientation, lines 55-75) and has no OUT analogue.

SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY. In the shipped v5 harness the gateway arm is always the real engine (harness.py:279, `gateway.restore_arguments`), so the real-run inflation is bounded by the leak rate rather than being 100% — but it is exactly the leaked population that becomes free hits in the four headline form lines, i.e. the instrument scores best where the product failed, and v4's δ for the same family was 3pp. Probe (3) is the sharper half: the tool leg trusts the engine's own residual dictionary (observe.py:436, 162-165) although the same file refuses to do that for the answer leg («the instrument reading the defendant's notes», docstring lines 28-35), and `substitute_surfaces` (observe.py:123-135) already gives the independent evidence needed.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED, with one correction to the example and one addition that makes it worse.

WHAT I RAN
1. The given reproduction, verbatim: `cd /Users/igor/Projects/Obscura/prototype && source .venv/bin/activate && PYTHONPATH=. python3 /Users/igor/.claude/jobs/4e5fce9b/tmp/metrics-lens/observe_probes.py`. Output reproduces the claim exactly: (d) raw «Передал Пахомовой Ольге, всё готово.» → restored «Передал Ивановой Елене, всё готово.» gives `answer_spans = ()`, OUT/answer `status=absent`, `answer_real 0/1`, `form_hOUT 0/0`; (d2) the reformatted phone gives the same.
2. My own probe, written independently: /Users/igor/.claude/jobs/4e5fce9b/tmp/verify-lens/probe.py. PHONE «+79990001122» → «+7 (999) 000-11-22», DOB «07.06.1979» → «7 июня 1979 года», LOC «улица Тихая 5» → «улицу Тихую 5» each read `absent` / `answer_real 0/1` / `form_hOUT 0/0`, while the echoed-verbatim controls read `observed` / 1/1 — so the probe separates its own zero from its own one.

MECHANISM (file:line)
- prototype/bench/agentpii5/observe.py:261-296 — `answer_spans` builds `needles` from `substitute_surfaces` ∪ `pieces_of`, and attributes a `replace` region only where a WHOLE needle `_occurrences` inside it.
- observe.py:123-133 `substitute_surfaces` = the minted surface + the surfaces MENTIONS recorded; harness.py:160-179 `_note_message_mentions` records exactly what the model READ at the item's span. A form the agent chose itself is in no needle set.
- observe.py:441-450 `_out_answer` → `absent` when no span carries the item; metrics.py:372-388 `answer_real` scores the answer a miss; metrics.py:349-355 `form_hOUT` drops the row from its DENOMINATOR (0/0), which is the v4 defect class the package's own ObserveError docstring condemns ("a denominator that moves with the data").

CORRECTION TO THE FINDING'S EXAMPLE
It is not true that any declension breaks it. A masculine genitive «Пахомов Олег» → «Пахомова Олега» IS attributed (the nominative is a prefix of the oblique). The defect fires only where the ending is REPLACED, not appended. Quantified over every NAME answer hop in corpus.v5.json using the engine's own morphology (`pseudex.morph_names.inflect_person`, script /Users/igor/.claude/jobs/4e5fce9b/tmp/verify-lens/scale2.py): 1168 of 2127 NAME answer hops (54.9%) lose the needle in at least one of gent/datv/ablt/accs — every feminine surname/given/patronymic («воронина»→«ворониной», «елена»→«елены», «сергеевна»→«сергеевны»), masculine given names in -й («сергей»→«сергея»), adjectival surnames («заболотный»→«заболотного»). PHONE (441 hops), DOB (548) and LOC (283) break on notation/agreement as shown in probe 2. Blast radius: 1215 of 1594 cases declare an answer hop, 3963 answer hops in total.

ADDITION — THE SAME ROOT FLATTERS, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC
Probe (e) in the given file: a declined substitute the engine did NOT restore stands in the customer's answer; `residual_answer_items` (observe.py:330-345, same whole-needle rule) returns frozenset() and `residual` (metrics.py:677-688) prints 2/2 CLEAN. docs/tz-agentpii5.md §4.3 calls that «подмена дошла до тула/ответа = критическая ошибка». So one half of the defect wrongly penalises a correct restoration (visible, implausibly low answer_real) and the other half hides a critical leak (invisible).

NOT BY DESIGN, NOT BY RULING
RULINGS.md:218 accepts "«answer_spans»' widening rules" only — nothing about the needle set; "«exists but no slot → absent»" is about tool slots and memory recall, not about a correctly restored answer. The package's own answer-leg test, test_observe.py:120-137, supplies the declined surface AS A MENTION («Кудрявцевой Диане»), i.e. it covers only the echo case; there is no fixture with a form the agent chose beyond what it was shown, so the report's refuse-to-report gate will not catch it.

UNVERIFIED (ranked last): how often a live Haiku agent actually writes a form outside the shown surfaces. No live model calls were permitted, so I measured the fragility of the corpus vocabulary and the observer's behaviour on hand-built records, not the agent's habit. The system prompt of the corpus cases («инициалы и латинское написание имени заполняй сам по ФИО», corpus.v5.json case chain-000) invites derived forms and nowhere asks for verbatim quoting.

SEVERITY: major, not blocker — nothing crashes and the corpus still runs; but three metrics named in the spec (answer_real, form_hOUT on the answer owner, residual on the answer) are systematically wrong on the majority of cases, and the residual half is wrong in the gateway's favour.

Because leak aggregates over the whole Sequence, absent hops in one case dilute a real leak in another: 1 leaked case + 4 idle -> 4/5 (80%), + 9 idle -> 9/10 (90%), with coverage steady at 0/1 — two lines of one report disagreeing about the population. Wrong under both readings of the spec: contracts.py:866 says the denominator is «all items shown to the model» (an absent hop showed nothing — coverage already excludes it at metrics.py:176-177), and docs/tz-agentpii5.md:309 («leak/coverage над всеми e») keeps it in the denominator but as a MISS, which is also what the module's own header demands at metrics.py:27 («an absent required hop is a MISS here, never a smaller total»). No ruling makes it deliberate: grep -i leak RULINGS.md returns only R-20 and R-35; the «Accepted as written» block after R-36 blesses observe.py PRODUCING absent and coverage's handling, never leak crediting it. Caveat for the architect, not against the finding: the proposed fix (exclude absent, mirroring coverage) matches contracts.py:866 but contradicts metrics.py:27 and spec §8.3, which argue for counting it as a miss with the denominator intact — coverage and the header already disagree, the choice must be applied to both lines, and the adversarial fixture must become a MIXED one (leaked + absent), since an all-100% fixture cannot separate the three candidate rules.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED, but materially narrower than the title claims — a real coverage gap on ~3 metrics, not "twelve wrong implementations defeat the gate's purpose".

WHAT I RAN
1. The given reproduction: `cd /Users/igor/Projects/Obscura/prototype && source .venv/bin/activate && PYTHONPATH=. python3 /Users/igor/.claude/jobs/4e5fce9b/tmp/metrics-lens/wrong_impls.py` — reproduces exactly: 12 wrong implementations print `printable=True`, only `stability_is_memory_stability` is refused (and that one only because it raises a TypeError, not because the fixtures separated it).
2. My own, decisive probe (/Users/igor/.claude/jobs/4e5fce9b/tmp/verify-fixture-gate/suite_probe.py): patch `metrics.METRIC_FUNCTIONS[<name>]` with the clause-dropping implementation and run the ENTIRE metric layer — `test_fixtures`, `test_metrics`, `test_report_gate` (which includes `report --selftest`, 27/27). For `end_to_end`, `multi_all_out` and `retry_form` all three modules print PASS: "OVERALL GREEN (nothing caught the wrong implementation)". So the gap is not merely in `gate`; nothing in the package pins the clause.

THE PART THAT SURVIVES
`prototype/bench/agentpii5/metrics.py:250` — `end_to_end`'s docstring is «the tool got the real value», and the body counts `hop.status == "observed" AND value_matches(...)`. Its three fixtures (`fixtures.py:357-374`) are: zero = an `absent` hop, one = right value, adversarial = one absent among two — every one of them varies only the STATUS. No fixture, and no test in `test_metrics.py` (`:181` asserts only `end_to_end`'s denominator, never its hits), has an observed hop carrying a WRONG value. An `end_to_end` that never reads the value therefore ships green, and under it a gateway that handed every tool the FAKE value would print 100% on the line the metric's own docstring calls one of «the two halves of the product's promise». Same shape, same probe result, for `multi_all_out` (`metrics.py:448` requires value AND form; `fixtures.py:597-615` breaks only the value, so a form-blind implementation passes) and `retry_form` (`metrics.py:520` says «EVERY attempt»; the zero fixture `fx-rf-0` at `fixtures.py:659-673` is right-then-wrong, so a last-attempt-only implementation passes all three). Three cheap fixtures close all three.

WHY I CUT IT DOWN FROM TWELVE, AND FROM «major»
- Nine of the twelve triples are EXACTLY what the spec prescribes. `docs/tz-agentpii5.md` §8.3 gives a per-metric fixture triple, and the code follows it verbatim: `form_h*` «падеж-сбой · точное совпадение · та же строка, но другой регистр» (fixtures.py:479-493), `toolresult_masked` «реал в результате · всё замаскировано · реал в тексте ошибки» (:496-519), `answer_real` «подмена · реал · реал в чужой форме» (:522), `chain_value` (:549), `memory_consistency` «перечеканено · одна · анафора без подмены» (:676-694), `multi_all_out` (:597), `retry_form` (:659), `rag_masked` (:724), `doc_masked` (:789). The builder did not deviate; the clauses the finding wants (a `leaked` hop in form_hIN's denominator, a partially-covering piece, a zero-mention MemorySpec) are not prescribed anywhere in the spec or in RULINGS.md. For those metrics this is a gap in the bar, not a violation of it.
- The method is partly tautological. Any finite fixture set can be defeated by an implementation written after reading it; several of the twelve are contrived rather than plausible — `chain_value_canonical_not_source` is indistinguishable in every fixture AND in `test_metrics.test_chain_transitions` because `source.reference` and `item.canonical` are the same string there; `overmask_any_message` and `form_hOUT_absent_in_denominator` drop clauses no builder would plausibly drop.
- The gate's own contract is met, and the headline overstates it. `report.py:85-107` + `contracts.py:917-919` declare exactly three kinds and separation ≥ 1.0; C-089/C-090/C-091 (CHECKLIST.md:109-111) demand three fixtures, a refusal on non-separation, and the `audit_gates --selftest` shape — and `report --selftest` genuinely refuses all 27 constant metrics. `INCOMPLETE_REPORT_MARK` exists for a metric that cannot separate its own zero from its own one, and it still does that. What is dented is C-008 (CHECKLIST.md:28, «every metric has a test that it counts correctly») for the three metrics above.
- Other layers do pin some of what the finding calls unpinned: `test_metrics.test_chain_transitions` (:105) pins chain_value's identity clause and its transition denominator, `test_rag_identity_kept` (:132) pins both mixing directions, `test_public_denominators` (:157) pins every public denominator.

Net: a genuine, verified, cheap-to-close hole on `end_to_end`, `multi_all_out`, `retry_form` — and `end_to_end` is the one worth fixing before the GO run, because the clause nothing pins is the product's central claim. The proposed fix is right in shape but should be scoped to those, not to twelve; nine of the twelve would be a change to the spec's §8.3 table first.

Built a one-turn two-call run with the package's fixture helpers (minted substitute «Пахомова Ольга», a MentionRecord carrying the dative «Пахомовой Ольге», call 1 writing the nominative into contact.name, call 2 writing the dative into a free-text note): metrics.multi_consistency returns Line(hits=0, total=1) — byte-identical to the control where the second call writes a DIFFERENT person's name (a genuine re-mint), while writing the same spelling twice returns 1/1. It is wrong by the spec: docs/tz-agentpii5.md:299 defines the line as «одно значение → одна подмена во всех вызовах» and §130-131 names the failure «перечеканена» (re-minted), not «spelled in another case»; inflecting the substitute to agree with the surrounding Russian is the engine's designed behaviour (CLAUDE.md #swap) that v5's own form_* family rewards, so this line scores the product down for what another line scores it up for. Not deliberate: I read RULINGS.md R-01…R-46 in full — no ruling mentions multi_consistency, substitute_surfaces, or spelling-vs-mint (R-05 covers form_match ABSTAIN only). No fixture can catch it: fixtures.py:618-641 builds zero/one/adversarial from FAKE_NAME vs OTHER_NAME (two different people) with the adversarial case being a retry at an IDENTICAL spelling, so an inflection never enters the gate.
